<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|392|THE EPISTLE OF S. PAVL|CHA. IIII.}}</noinclude>the father of vs al, {{verse|chapter=4|verse=17}}† (as it is vvritten: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 17, 4.''}}* ''For, a father of many nations haue I appointed thee'') before God, vvhom {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''`he beleeued,''}}`thou didst beleeue', vvho quickeneth the dead: and calleth those things that are not, as those things that are. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=18}}† VVho contrarie to hope beleeued in hope: that he might be made the father of many nations, according to that vvhich vvas {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 15, 5.''}}* said to him: ''So shal thy seede be'', as the starres of heauen, and the sand of the sea. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=19}}† And he vvas not vveakened in faith: neither did he consider his ovvne body novv quite dead, vvhereas he vvas almost an hundred yeres old, and the dead matrice of Sara. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=20}}† In the promisse also of God he staggered not by distrust: but vvas strengthened in faith, giuing glorie to God: {{verse|chapter=4|verse=21}}† most fully knovving that vvhatsoeuer he promised, he is able also to doe. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=22}}† Therfore vvas it also reputed him to iustice.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=23}}† And it is not vvritten only for him, that it vvas reputed him to iustice: {{verse|chapter=4|verse=24}}† but also {{sup|‖}} for vs, to vvhom it shal be reputed beleeuing in him, that raised vp {{sc|Iesvs Christ}} our Lord from the dead, {{verse|chapter=4|verse=25}}† vvho vvas deliuered vp for our sinnes, and rose againe for our iustification.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. IIII.}}}}

''1. Abraham.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Abrahams workes before faith.}}The Apostle disputing in this chapter, as before, against them that thought they might be iustified by their vvorkes done vvithout the grace of Christ and faith in him, proposeth Abraham for an example, and proueth that he had no other estimation of iustice before God by any vvorkes done before his faith, or that proceeded not of faith and Gods grace.

''2. By vvorkes.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Iustice before men, and iustice before God.}}If Abraham did any commendable workes before he beleeued Christ, as many Philosophers did, men might count him wel therfore, but in Gods light (who accepteth nothing without faith in him, or that proceedeth not from his grace) he should neuer haue had the estimation of a iust man. Therfore God in the Scriptures reputing him as a iust man, giueth the cause therof, saying, ''Abraham beleeued God, and it vvas reputed to him for iustice''.

''4. To him that worketh.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Not workes, but mere grace is cause of our first iustification.}}That is to say, He that presumeth of his ovvne vvorkes as done of him self without faith, Gods helpe and grace: and saying, that grace or iustification were giuen to him for his workes: this man doth chalenge his iustification as dette, and not as of fauour and grace.

''5. To him that worketh not.''] He worketh not (in this place) that hath no workes or alleageth not his workes done in his infidelitie as cause of his iustification, but faith in Christ, and that proceding of mere grace. Vvherevpon S. Augustine saith: ''Know thou that faith found thee vniust. And if faith giuen to thee, made thee iust, it found thee a vvicked one vvhom it might make iust. If it found thee wicked, and of such an one made thee iust, vvhat vvorkes hadst thou being then vvicked? None couldest thou haue (nor canst haue) before thou beleeuedst. Beleeue then in him that iustifieth the impious, that thy good vvorkes may be good workes in deede''. August. in Psal. 31.

''6. As Dauid termeth.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Heretical translation.}}The Protestants for, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''c λέγει''}}''termeth'', translate, ''describeth'', for that they vvould haue the ignorant beleeue, the vvhole nature & definition of Iustification to be nothing els but remission of sinnes, and no grace or inherent iustice giuen from God at al. When the Apostle would say nothing els, but that in the first iustification God findeth no good workes or merites to revvard, but only sinnes to forgiue vnto such as haue faith in him.

''7. Couered. 8. not imputed.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=What is, ''Sinne couered or not imputed''.}}You may not gather (as the Heretikes doe) of these termes, ''couered'', and, ''not imputed'', that the sinnes of men be neuer truely forgiuen, but hidden only. for that derogateth much to the force of Christes bloud and to the grace of God, by which our offences be<noinclude>{{rh|||truely}}</noinclude>
